sections.content: How many people are "public relations and communications directors"?

20,035 people

were counted on the census as "public relations and communications directors" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Public relations and communications directors organise and direct the public relations, communications and public information activities of an organisation or on behalf of clients.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 40 to 44 years. Of the whole working population 10.9% were aged 40 to 44 years. For people working as "public relations and communications directors", 17.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "public relations and communications directors" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "public relations and communications directors" included:

  • specialist medical practitioners
  • functional managers and directors (other)
  • information technology directors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "public relations and communications directors" there were a similar number of men and women (53.5% compared with 46.5%).

This means "public relations and communications directors" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 53.5% and women made up 46.5% of "public relations and communications directors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "public relations and communications directors" included:

  • newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters
  • shelf fillers
  • debt, rent and other cash collectors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "public relations and communications directors", 6.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (84.7% compared with 15.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (75.9%) than self-employed (24.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wandsworth, this is in the same region of London.
